phase: Phase 1.3 - the database: SQLite in each project directory
exit_criterion: The five JSON indexes and the executor's cache index are gone from a project directory, replaced by project.db; the full suite and the Playwright walkthrough pass unchanged on all three platforms; and a project directory written by v0.3.0 still opens. Endpoints, payloads and the frontend are untouched - what the database unlocks (many pipelines, an experiment history, pagination, a project browser) is deliberately after this phase, not in it.

features.title: The database module: one SQLite file per project directory
features.user_visible_behavior: A project directory holds a project.db. Opening one written by a newer version of the application is refused by name rather than misread.
verification: A new project directory gets a project.db whose PRAGMA user_version reads back 1.
A database stamped user_version = 2 is refused, and the message names both numbers.
PRAGMA journal_mode reads back wal.
uv run ruff check && uv run ruff format --check && uv run mypy && uv run pytest
features.evidence: 2026-08-29. `uv run pytest tests/test_db.py` - 9 passed: the database is created inside the project directory, a new one is stamped user_version 1, all seven tables are written, a database stamped user_version 2 is refused with both numbers and the path in the message, a directory with no database is an error rather than an empty project, PRAGMA journal_mode reads back wal with foreign_keys=1 and busy_timeout=5000, one engine serves a directory however its path is spelled, reopening does not rewrite, and a session round-trips a row. `CHEMOMETRICS_DOWNLOAD_DATASETS=1 uv run pytest` - 745 passed, 1 skipped. `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` clean; `uv run mypy` - no issues in 47 source files.
features.notes: src/chemometrics_workbench/db.py, plus SQLAlchemy in [project.dependencies] - a runtime dependency, because the application cannot open a project without it. Four decisions come from docs/decisions/0002-phase-1-shape.md lines 57-67 and are not re-argued: one database per project at <project_dir>/project.db; tables hold identity, the queried columns and the Pydantic model as JSON, because models.py is the schema of record and mirroring twenty classes creates two sources of truth; no Alembic, create_all plus a user_version guard; the float32 store boundary unchanged. Nothing calls the module in this feature - project.py still writes JSON until #120. Implemented 2026-08-29: sqlalchemy>=2.0 in [project.dependencies] (2.0.52 locked, greenlet beside it). DatabaseError lives in db.py rather than reusing project.ProjectError, because project.py imports db and the reverse would be a cycle; both mean the same thing and both name the path. Timestamps are ISO-8601 strings and ids are strings, for the engine portability PROPOSAL.md section 12 commits to; the document column is the model's own JSON, so nothing is queried inside it. Layout is its own table rather than a column on pipeline, so moving a node writes a different row than the one the content hash is computed from.

features.title: project.py reads and writes through the database
features.user_visible_behavior: The project's index is the database: datasets, the pipeline, its layout and the last experiment survive a restart from tables rather than from five JSON files. Nothing the user sees changes.
verification: tests/test_project.py - the zip-and-open portability test passes unchanged.
tests/test_project.py - no absolute path is recorded anywhere in the project.
tests/test_api.py - the restart round-trip lists the identical dataset.
tests/test_server.py - the pipeline reads back after a module-reload restart.
cd frontend && npx playwright test - 38 tests over four seeded projects.
features.evidence: 2026-08-29. `uv run pytest` - 745 passed, 1 skipped, the same count as before the swap: the tests that named the five JSON files now name the database and assert the same invariants. The three that matter for portability pass unchanged - no absolute path anywhere in project.db's own bytes, the round trip through a subprocess, and zip the directory, extract it elsewhere, delete the original, open it. `cd frontend && npx playwright test` - 38 passed across seeded, empty, runs and walkthrough, against a backend whose index is now SQLite. `uv run ruff check`, `uv run ruff format --check` and `uv run mypy` all clean.
features.notes: project.json, datasets.json, pipeline.json, pipeline_layout.json and experiment.json become tables. arrays/<sha256>.npy and results/<key>.json stay files - PROPOSAL.md section 11 says the database stores references, never contents, and a fitted result is contents. The config directory registry stays too: it is the one thing a project directory cannot know, that the user has it. Every public signature in project.py stays exactly as it is, so api.py, executor.py, server.py and tests/seed_e2e.py are untouched; a signature that has to change is a finding worth an issue, not a widened branch. add_dataset's unlocked read-modify-write (project.py:268-297) becomes one insert in one transaction - the first real bug the database fixes. Implemented 2026-08-29. Every public signature stayed as it was, so executor.py, server.py and tests/seed_e2e.py are untouched; api.py changed in one place only, and not a signature - it decided create-or-open by asking whether project.json existed, which is a fact about the directory layout, so it now asks project.is_project(). _read_model and _read_json were deleted with the last JSON reader; #121 brings back what it needs. read_experiment returns the most recently started row rather than the one file's contents, which gives an experiment history nothing reads yet. write_layout is keyed on the project's pipeline and refuses a layout with no pipeline to belong to. ExperimentRow.started_at became nullable, because Experiment types it so: a pending run has not started.

features.title: A project directory written before the database opens
features.user_visible_behavior: A project directory created by v0.3.0 opens and reads back identically, without the user re-importing anything.
verification: A project directory seeded by v0.3.0's own code opens, and everything it held reads back.
cd frontend && npx playwright test - 38 passed, the seeded projects unaffected.
uv run pytest - the reader accepts the shape v0.3.0 wrote, twice over without importing twice.
features.evidence: 2026-08-29. Checked out v0.3.0 in a worktree and seeded a project with *its* code (PYTHONPATH ahead of the editable install, confirmed by the module path and by is_project being absent): the directory came out with project.json, datasets.json, pipeline.json, pipeline_layout.json, experiment.json, arrays/ and no database. Opening it with this branch read back the project (Tecator meat study), the dataset (tecator_raw, 240 x 100, its array_path intact), the 14-node pipeline with content hash sha256:62ece5b6d8424835..., the layout, and the succeeded experiment; project.db was created and all six JSON files were still on disk. `uv run pytest` - 753 passed, 1 skipped, including 8 new in tests/test_project_json_import.py. `cd frontend && npx playwright test` - 38 passed. ruff, format and mypy clean over 48 files.
features.notes: open_project reads the five JSON files once into a fresh database in one transaction and leaves them in place, never read again. One function, one test, deleted in a later phase. Not a clean break, because the seeded e2e projects and any developer's directory are real users of the old shape; not a two-way sync either. Implemented 2026-08-29. is_project() had to count a JSON directory too, or api.py would have sent it to create_project, which refuses over an existing project. The import found a real ordering bug: without a declared relationship between the two mappers, SQLAlchemy's unit of work attempted the pipeline_layout insert before the pipeline it points at and the foreign key refused it - one flush between them, with the reason recorded. An unreadable file is named rather than skipped: a project whose pipeline will not parse has lost work, and starting again from nothing is the wrong answer to that.

features.title: The executor's cache index moves into the database
features.user_visible_behavior: Re-running an unchanged pipeline still recomputes nothing, and editing one node still recomputes only that node and its descendants - with no JSON index left in the project.
verification: tests/test_executor.py - a second run recomputes nothing; an edit recomputes the node and its descendants only; an edit below a split leaves the branch above.
tests/test_executor.py - a pruned .npy is recomputed rather than refused; use_cache=False neither reads nor writes the index.
A cache entry naming a missing array costs a recomputation, which is what the corrupt-cache.json test becomes.
features.evidence: 2026-08-29. `uv run pytest` - 754 passed, 1 skipped. The executor's cache claims pass in table form: a second run recomputes nothing, an edit recomputes the node and its descendants only, an edit below a split leaves the branch above, a pruned .npy is recomputed rather than refused, and use_cache=False leaves read_cache_index empty. The corrupt-cache.json test became 'an index entry naming a missing array costs a recomputation', which is the failure that can still happen now the index is rows. Measured on a project seeded by v0.3.0's own code: its cache.json held 10 entries, the table held the identical 10 after opening, and a run on the migrated project reused all 10 and recomputed 0. `cd frontend && npx playwright test` - 38 passed. ruff, format and mypy clean over 48 files.
features.notes: cache.json is a map from a node's cache key to the array paths it produced - pure references, which is what the database is for. The ponytail note at executor.py:908-910 (the index only grows, no mark-and-sweep) stays true and stays marked. One transaction per run rather than per node only if a measurement says the per-node cost matters. Implemented 2026-08-29. The accessors live in project.py as read_cache_index and write_cache_index, beside the other store functions, rather than in executor.py reaching into the database itself - the executor has always gone through project.py for storage. cache.json is also read across by #121's import: without it every node in a migrated project would recompute, which is correct but a pipeline's worth of work to arrive back where the project already was.

features.title: Two processes over one project directory
features.user_visible_behavior: A second application instance on the same project directory reads without blocking and writes without corrupting; a write that cannot get the lock says which project it was waiting for.
verification: Two engines on one directory, both writing, both sets of rows present afterwards.
A write held past busy_timeout produces the named error, not a bare 'database is locked'.
tests/test_server.py - concurrent reads never fail, still passes.
features.notes: api.py:186-191 defers exactly this to 1.3, and docs/phase-1-2/feature_list.json:50 records it as undefined until a database can arbitrate. WAL plus busy_timeout is the answer. The in-process _CREATE_LOCK at api.py:168 stays: it guards a check-then-create inside one process, which is a different problem.

features.title: The phase closes: the documents match the repository, and a tag
features.user_visible_behavior: A reader of the documents finds the repository they describe, and the release line carries the phase.
verification: The full suite green on all three platforms, which is the pull request's own CI.
By hand: open a project, run a pipeline, kill the server, start it again - datasets, pipeline and last experiment are all still there.
features.notes: CLAUDE.md loses the sentence about a restart losing the project list. design/data-model.md records the tables and fixes a filename mismatch: the documents say pipeline_state.json (session-handoff.md:240, executor.py:44), the code says pipeline_layout.json (project.py:90), and after this phase it is a table with neither name. 0002-phase-1-shape.md gets a note that its four database decisions were implemented as written. pyproject.toml still says 0.2.0 although v0.3.0 is tagged. Then dev into main, and v0.4.0.
